datafield.subfield: A miniature alphabet book. "The word grammar has several meanings. There is the common understanding of grammar as the study of syntax and other guidelines of written language; and then less common in our era is a grammar, a textbookdelineating the rules of grammar. More broadly, grammar can refer to "the principle or rules of an art, science, or technique." Grammar itself is the root of the word glamor-- a magic spell-- a Scottish variation of grammar that derives from " the popular association of erudition with occult practives." Thus, grammar as language, as rules, as art, as science, as sorcery. Sources: the definition of grammar and the etymology of glamour are taken from the Merriam-Webster Dictionary; the illustration for Demiurge is based on William Blake's Ancient of Days; the epigraph on the title page is from Charles Fort's Lo!" from colophon.
